statement: BC should approve new liquefied natural gas (LNG) export projects.

passages.title: David Eby secures largest private sector investment in Canadian history
passages.quote: That agreement sets British Columbia on a generational path to prosperity, unlocking jobs for workers, generating revenue for vital public services and infrastructure, and protecting the tanker ban and British Columbia’s pristine northern coast. The BC Conservatives opposed the agreement when it was signed. B.C.’s natural gas is among the lowest-emission LNG in the world. Emissions from this project are projected to be 35% lower than the world's best-performing LNG facilities and 60% lower than the global average.

passages.title: David Eby bets big on potential for more major projects in Build B.C. Strong platform (Vancouver Sun)
passages.quote: “They don’t do that when things are bad.” Article content Eby made the election call on the heels of Victoria and Ottawa granting an environmental green light for FortisBC’s $3.5 billion Tilbury liquefied natural gas expansion, which has the prospect of creating more than 1,000 jobs in the Lower Mainland during its construction and add $1.7 billion to B.C.’s gross domestic product. passages.quote: Our success here is the envy of many jurisdictions across Canada and around the world, but we do this as British Columbians to support the entire country. We are excited about the opportunities in energy — LNG Canada phase 2. Reflecting on our accounts, somewhere around $80 billion of investment related to energy projects and 5,000 new trades-training seats so British Columbians are at the front of the line to take those jobs. The happy news, just yesterday, is that our work here in British Columbia is supporting people in Germany that have shut off their access to Russian natural gas and have signed a $10 billion agreement with Ksi Lisims LNG to access B.C.

passages.title: David Eby secures largest private sector investment in Canadian history
passages.quote: "This is a big win that will create good jobs and generate the long-term prosperity we need to deliver stronger public services for all British Columbians," said David Eby. "We are seeing real momentum in B.C., but the job isn’t done – we need to keep going. Conservative chaos, reckless cuts, and a willingness to walk away from what is clearly working would put these nation-building projects at risk and leave everyday people paying the price." Eby noted that projects like LNG Canada rely on strong partnerships with First Nations, and that B.C.’s low-emitting natural gas is what attracts countries like Germany, Japan, and Australia as customers.
